newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip on slight profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip on slight profit-taking.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly lower Friday as the market shook off its last bout of profit-taking this week, traders said.
Prices rose early on the back of firm U.S. Treasuries after subdued U.S. producer price figures but a lack of market activity ahead of the weekend left the market to languish lower in the afternoon.
"The market has fallen this week in a technical correction in preparation for likely new positions next week," said Hugo Diaz Lourenco, senior analyst at financial consultancy C&E Consultores.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slipped $0.05 to 119.10, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1/4 to 83-1/4.
Longer-dated bonds were harder hit, with the dollar-denominated Bocon Provisional due 2007 down $0.60 to 103.70.

A general sensation in the market that the economy is poised for a pick-up in growth and that the government will push through its labor reforms is expected to underpin the bond market in the coming week.
"In the short-term, there are no upsetting bits of news anticipated," said another analyst.

He added that the monthly payments to the private pension funds from new members will take place next week, something that could help support the market since the funds are obliged to invest a large portion of funds in bonds.
In the money markets, call money rose to 6.50 percent from 6.45 percent.
